brief: A competition has been announced for a new international Arctic Centre in Vatnsmýri, alongside an open house for the Sæbraut tunnel project. In Vestmannaeyjar, Litla-Hraun has been demolished, and an archaeological dig is underway at the site of Laugavegur's oldest house. Elsewhere, a data breach at the District Prosecutor's office is under investigation by Persónuvernd. A Chinese billionaire received a 30-year sentence in the US, and there are reports of an impending challenge to Hvalur hf.'s oil company.

items.title: Kínverskur milljarðamæringur dæmdur í 30 ára fangelsi í Bandaríkjunum
items.summary: Chinese billionaire Guo Wengui has been sentenced to 30 years in a US prison for fraud, extortion, and money laundering. He defrauded thousands of followers of over a billion dollars, using the money to fund his lavish lifestyle.

items.title: Fær ekki að reka Cook úr bankaráði seðlabankans
items.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled against Donald Trump's attempt to remove Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve Board, citing a lack of due process. Trump had accused Cook of financial misconduct, but she maintained the accusations were politically motivated due to her monetary policy decisions. This marks the first time a US president has tried to fire a Fed board member.
items.why_matters: This ruling reinforces the independence of the US Federal Reserve, which is vital for maintaining stable monetary policy free from political interference.

items.title: Fjárfestingarfélagið orðið eins og lítill lífeyrissjóður á Íslandi
items.summary: The article highlights the growing influence of the Icelandic investment company Stoðir, a major shareholder in key businesses like the merging Blue Lagoon and Arctic Adventures. A financial analyst compares Stoðir's 53 billion ISK in investment assets to a small pension fund, noting its role as an "influence investor" due to its significant stakes and board representation. Stoðir is also undertaking one of Iceland's largest private investments in land-based salmon farming.
items.why_matters: This article details the significant and growing influence of a major investment company on the Icelandic economy, impacting various key sectors and future development.

items.title: Öryggisbrestur hjá héraðssaksóknara á borði Persónuverndar
items.summary: A security breach at the District Prosecutor's office in Iceland is under investigation by the Data Protection Authority. Names and case numbers of five individuals under criminal investigation were inadvertently revealed in a promotional video created by an Israeli company. The incident highlights concerns about data protection within the justice system.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights vulnerabilities in data protection within the Icelandic justice system, potentially compromising ongoing investigations and the privacy of individuals.

items.title: Bandero boðar atlögu að olíufélagi Hvals hf.
items.summary: The Paul Watson organization's ship, Bandero, currently in Icelandic waters, has announced plans to target the oil company that services the Icelandic whaling company Hvalur hf. The organization aims to stop whaling, claiming one of the recently caught fin whales was pregnant. The Icelandic coast guard vessel Þór is monitoring Bandero.
items.why_matters: This direct action could disrupt whaling operations and potentially lead to confrontations with authorities or legal action.

items.title: Svavar Pálsson ráðinn sveitarstjóri Húnabyggðar
items.summary: Svavar Pálsson has been appointed as the new municipal manager for Húnabyggð, taking office on October 1st. He brings extensive experience in public administration and local ties, aiming to continue the development and growth of the municipality.
items.why_matters: This appointment will influence the future planning and development decisions within the Húnabyggð municipality.

items.title: Hugmyndir Evrópusambandsins óspennandi
items.summary: Iceland's Foreign Minister, Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir, finds proposed EU changes to limit veto power for new member states unappealing, potentially making accession less attractive. She acknowledges the EU's reasons for considering such safeguards, especially after Hungary's actions, and discusses the rationale for Iceland to consider starting EU accession talks.
items.why_matters: This discussion could significantly influence Iceland's future relationship with the European Union and its geopolitical standing.

items.title: „Þetta eru spennandi tímar“
items.summary: A new health spa is under construction in Siglufjörður, designed by Former arkitektar and connected to the Segull 67 craft brewery. The spa will feature unique design elements, including geothermal-heated basalt sand baths and a sea spring utilizing marine ingredients. The project faces a challenge due to the government's proposed VAT increase on spa services.
items.why_matters: The proposed VAT increase could impact the viability of new tourism and wellness projects like this spa, affecting local businesses and regional development.

items.title: Samgöngurnar verið betri í sumar
items.summary: The mayor of Vestmannaeyjar reports that ferry services have improved this summer compared to last winter, despite recent disruptions. However, she emphasizes the ongoing challenges with the Herjólfur ferry and Landeyjahöfn port, calling for increased funding for dredging and the construction of a new, larger ferry. The issue requires government intervention to ensure reliable transportation for the islands.
items.why_matters: Reliable ferry and port services are vital for the economy and residents of Vestmannaeyjar, impacting their daily lives and access to the mainland.
items.spin_note: The headline suggests a largely positive situation, but the article details significant ongoing problems and calls for major government intervention and new infrastructure.

items.title: Langþráð reglugerð um lyfjaakstur á næstu grösum
items.summary: The Ministry of Infrastructure is finalizing a long-awaited regulation on driving under the influence of prescription drugs, setting specific impairment limits for 21 medications. This development follows criticism from a lawyer regarding legal uncertainty and past wrongful convictions due to the absence of clear guidelines since traffic laws changed six years ago. Various organizations have provided feedback on the draft, with some welcoming the clarity and others raising concerns about its scope and comparison to the Norwegian model.
items.why_matters: This regulation aims to provide legal clarity for drivers and law enforcement, preventing wrongful convictions and ensuring fair application of laws regarding driving under the influence of prescription medication.

items.title: Öskjuhlíðartré efniviður í nýja þorpinu
items.summary: A new residential area called Hamborg is under development in Fljótsdalshreppur, East Iceland, with the local municipality initiating the construction of the first house. This house is notable as it's the first in Iceland built using Icelandic timber, sourced from trees felled in Öskjuhlíð, Reykjavík. The project aims to address a local housing shortage and promote the use of domestic wood products.
items.why_matters: This municipal project addresses a housing shortage and demonstrates a new approach to construction using local resources, potentially influencing future building practices.

items.title: Gefur lítið fyrir „anti everything-liðið“
items.summary: Nine fin whales have been caught this season, while anti-whaling activist Paul Watson's ship has entered Icelandic waters. The Icelandic Coast Guard is monitoring the situation and has postponed its 100-year anniversary celebrations due to the ongoing surveillance. The CEO of the whaling company dismisses the activists.
items.why_matters: This situation involves potential conflict between activists and whalers, requiring intervention from the Icelandic Coast Guard, and has led to the postponement of a significant national event.

items.title: Andlát: Halldór Haraldsson
items.summary: Halldór Haraldsson, a prominent Icelandic pianist and music educator, has passed away at 89. He was instrumental in Icelandic music education, serving as a director at the Reykjavík College of Music and helping establish the Iceland University of the Arts. He also performed extensively and founded several music organizations.

items.title: Hluti af sorgarferlinu að sjá húsið rifið
items.summary: The article focuses on Halldóra Birta Viðarsdóttir, a former resident of Grindavík, as she witnesses the demolition of her family's ancestral home. The house on Víkurbraut was severely damaged by the geological events in 2023, making it uninhabitable. Halldóra shares her emotional journey and the profound sense of loss associated with seeing her home destroyed.
items.why_matters: This article illustrates the personal and emotional toll of the Grindavík disaster on residents whose homes are being demolished.

items.title: Með kylfur í hendi og mikið magn fíkniefna
items.summary: The article details incidents from the capital region police log, including an arrest for assault and robbery. It also reports on three individuals caught with clubs and a large quantity of drugs, who will face charges for weapons violations and drug possession.
items.why_matters: It informs residents about ongoing crime and law enforcement activity in the capital region.

items.title: Hyggst ekki semja um sjávarútveginn
items.summary: The article criticizes Foreign Minister Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir's approach to potential EU accession talks, specifically regarding fisheries. The author argues that her reliance on the EU's "relative stability" rule would not secure Iceland's sovereignty over its fishing resources, as ultimate control would transfer to Brussels. It highlights that this rule is not a permanent or legally robust safeguard within EU treaties.
items.why_matters: This discussion directly impacts Iceland's potential future relationship with the EU and the sovereignty over its vital fishing industry.

items.title: Gagnaleki héraðssaksóknara rannsakaður
items.summary: The Icelandic Data Protection Authority is investigating a serious data leak from the District Prosecutor's office. Names of five individuals under criminal investigation were inadvertently displayed in a promotional video, which has since been removed. This breach is considered a security incident with potential legal penalties.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights critical issues with data security and accountability within government institutions, potentially impacting individuals' privacy and trust in the justice system.

items.title: Boða atlögu að olíufélagi Hvals hf.
items.summary: Paul Watson's conservation group, Bandero, announced plans to target the oil company that services the Icelandic whaling company Hvalur hf. This action follows Hvalur 9 landing two fin whales, one reportedly pregnant, in Hvalfjörður. The Icelandic Coast Guard is monitoring Bandero, which is currently outside territorial waters but within Iceland's economic zone.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights ongoing international pressure on Icelandic whaling and could lead to confrontations or legal action, impacting the whaling industry and potentially international relations.

items.title: Árni og Sara keyptu hús í Hafnarfirði
items.summary: Icelandic football stars Sara Björk Gunnarsdóttir and Árni Vilhjálmsson have purchased a 251.9 sqm semi-detached house in Hafnarfjörður for 165 million ISK. They also sold their 112 sqm apartment in Garðabær for 90.8 million ISK. The article briefly mentions Sara Björk's recent return to Iceland after playing professionally in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Hótel Siglunes falt fyrir 490 milljónir
items.summary: Hótel Siglunes, a historic hotel in Siglufjörður built in 1934, is now listed for sale at 490 million ISK. The property, which includes 17 rooms, two staff apartments, and several adjacent plots, was extensively renovated a decade ago to preserve its charm and history. It offers a unique investment opportunity with potential for further development.

items.title: Litla-Hraun í Vestmannaeyjum jafnað við jörðu
items.summary: Demolition has begun on Litla-Hraun, one of the oldest residential houses in Vestmannaeyjar, built in 1911. The Vestmannaeyjar Environment and Planning Council approved its demolition last year after the Cultural Heritage Agency of Iceland deemed the neglected house beyond repair. The house had historical significance, including being featured in the film Djúpið.
items.why_matters: This planning decision by the Vestmannaeyjar council results in the loss of a historic building, impacting local architectural heritage.

items.title: Fornleifauppgröftur á lóð elsta húss Laugavegar
items.summary: An archaeological excavation is currently underway at Laugavegur 1, the site of one of Reykjavík's oldest houses, which was recently demolished. The building, originally constructed in 1848, is being rebuilt to its original form, with archaeologists uncovering 19th-century artifacts. Efforts will be made to reuse as much of the original building material as possible.

items.title: Fyrirhuguð samkeppni um nýjan alþjóðlegan Norðurslóðakjarna í Vatnsmýrinni
items.summary: An international architectural competition has been announced for a new 20,000 square meter Arctic Hub in Vatnsmýri, Reykjavík. This building will serve as a global center for research, innovation, and cooperation on Arctic issues, strengthening Iceland's role in the region.
items.why_matters: This project will significantly impact the Vatnsmýri area's development and solidify Iceland's international standing in Arctic affairs.

items.title: Sæbraut­ar­stokkur – Opið hús í Voga­­skóla
items.summary: Reykjavík City, the Road Administration, and Better Transport are hosting an open house for the Sæbraut Tunnel project, a key part of the Capital Region Transport Agreement. The project involves a nearly 1 km tunnel with a new green park above it, aiming to improve traffic flow, connect neighborhoods, and facilitate future public transport.
items.why_matters: This project will significantly alter traffic flow, connect neighborhoods, and facilitate future public transport and freight, impacting daily life and urban development in the capital region.

items.title: Gólfhiti í nýjum húsum skapar kjöraðstæður fyrir silfurskottur til að fjölga sér
items.summary: New houses, particularly those with underfloor heating and timber construction, are creating ideal conditions for silverfish to thrive and multiply. A pest control expert notes an increase in calls for silverfish in newer homes, attributing it to factors like underfloor heating and building materials. While common, the issue is treatable and not a cause for panic.

items.title: 59 þúsund byggingar gætu hafa skemmst eða eyðilagst
items.summary: NASA estimates that nearly 59,000 buildings were damaged or destroyed in powerful earthquakes that struck Venezuela last week. The disaster has resulted in over 1,700 deaths, 5,000 injuries, and 15,000 people losing their homes. Additionally, more than 43,000 individuals are still reported missing.
items.why_matters: This disaster highlights the devastating impact of natural catastrophes on infrastructure and human lives globally.

items.title: Árós Pípulagnir auglýsa eftir verkamanni
items.summary: Árós Pípulagnir, a plumbing company, is seeking a construction worker to join their team due to an increase in projects. The role involves general labor, assistance with installation and finishing, material handling, and site maintenance on various construction sites.

items.title: Fósturfaðir grunaður um ítrekuð kynferðisbrot gegn barni áfram í haldi
items.summary: A 40-year-old man in Suðurnes, suspected of repeatedly sexually abusing a foster child in his care, has been remanded in custody until July 22. The police investigation is ongoing and currently focuses on offenses against one primary school-aged child.
items.why_matters: This case highlights serious child protection concerns within the foster care system in Iceland.

items.title: Bíddu ha? á BKPM plötu vikunnar?
items.summary: The article introduces the Icelandic band BKPM and their debut album "Bíddu ha?". It details the band's formation, members, and their experimental post-punk style, noting their appearance on RÚV's "Plata vikunnar" to discuss their work.

items.title: Tóku hátt í 200 kannabisplöntur í Reykholti
items.summary: Police in South Iceland seized nearly 200 cannabis plants and cultivation equipment in Reykholt, Bláskógabyggð. This is considered one of the largest drug cultivations in the region in recent years. One person was arrested in connection with the case, which is under investigation for potential links to organized crime.
items.why_matters: This significant drug bust highlights ongoing efforts by Icelandic police to combat large-scale illegal drug production and distribution.

items.title: Ráðherra eigi að gæta betur hagsmuna eigin kjördæmis
items.summary: The ferry Baldur, vital for the Breiðafjörður area, was diverted to Vestmannaeyjar, causing significant disruption to local communities and tourism. Local authorities and residents are criticizing the Minister of Infrastructure for this decision, citing reduced service, negative economic impact, and lack of consultation. The ferry's return has been repeatedly delayed.
items.why_matters: This government decision to divert a critical ferry service is causing significant economic losses for local tourism businesses and disrupting daily life and essential services for residents in the Breiðafjörður region.

items.title: Samningur um háskólasamstæðu undirritaður
items.summary: An agreement was signed to merge Hólaskóli with the University of Iceland, forming Iceland's first university consortium. This follows parliamentary approval earlier this month, with the new structure taking effect on July 1st.
items.why_matters: This establishes Iceland's first university consortium, representing a significant structural change in the country's higher education system.

items.title: Edition-málið: Höfðu hvorki sofið né borðað í nær tvo sólarhringa
items.summary: The article reports on the ongoing trial of Ming Ting Mancel, who is accused of killing her daughter Catherine in collaboration with her husband at the Edition hotel in Reykjavík. Mancel testified that her daughter asked her father to stab her again after the initial attempt, and that the family had come to Iceland to die together due to the husband's fatal illness. The court heard details about the husband's internet search history regarding suicide methods.
items.why_matters: This is a significant domestic criminal case with ongoing legal proceedings.

items.title: Fresta frekari viðgerðum á brúnni yfir Jökulsá á Fjöllum fram yfir mesta ferðatíma
items.summary: The Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration has postponed further maintenance work on the bridge over Jökulsá á Fjöllum until August 17th. The delay is due to heavy rain, and the decision was made to avoid disrupting peak summer travel. The bridge, built in 1947, needs repairs to address rust and maintain its load-bearing capacity.
items.why_matters: The postponement of bridge repairs affects travel plans for those using the route and highlights ongoing infrastructure maintenance needs.

items.title: Ekki tilefni til að endurskoða lyfjaakstursmál
items.summary: The State Prosecutor has decided not to review past cases of driving under the influence of prescription drugs, despite a lawyer's call for it after a recent appeals court ruling. Meanwhile, the Ministry of Infrastructure is developing new regulations to clarify impairment limits for such cases.
items.why_matters: This decision affects the legal standing of past convictions and clarifies how driving under prescription drugs will be handled in the future.

items.title: Lönduðu tveimur langreyðum
items.summary: The whaling ship Hvalur 9 landed two fin whales in Hvalfjörður, bringing the season's total to nine. An anti-whaling protest ship, Bandero, has entered Icelandic waters with the stated aim of disrupting whaling, and is being monitored by the Icelandic Coast Guard.
items.why_matters: This situation highlights ongoing tensions surrounding whaling in Iceland, involving international activism and national enforcement.

items.title: „Reiðubúnir að leggja lífið að veði“
items.summary: An international anti-whaling group, Sea Shepherd, has deployed its ship 'Bandero' off the coast of Iceland, with crew members stating they are prepared for prolonged, non-violent direct action to stop whaling. The Icelandic Coast Guard is monitoring the vessel, and the situation has led to the cancellation of the Coast Guard's 100th-anniversary celebration. The expedition leader has a history of sabotaging Icelandic whaling operations in 1986.
items.why_matters: This incident involves a direct confrontation between an international activist group and Icelandic authorities, impacting public events and potentially the whaling industry.

items.title: Kannabisræktunin í Reykholti hluti af stærri rannsókn
items.summary: Police in South Iceland uncovered a large-scale cannabis cultivation operation in Reykholt, seizing nearly 200 plants and equipment. Authorities suspect this operation is linked to two other recent cannabis busts in the southwest region and involves organized crime.
items.why_matters: This highlights ongoing efforts by Icelandic police to combat organized crime and drug production within the country.

items.title: Trump fær ekki að reka Cook
items.summary: The US Supreme Court blocked former President Donald Trump's attempt to immediately fire Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve Board. Trump had accused Cook of mortgage fraud and sought to remove her to influence the Fed's interest rate policy. The court ruled that presidents cannot fire independent central bank officials without due process.
items.why_matters: The independence of the US Federal Reserve and its ability to set interest rates without political interference has global economic implications, including for smaller economies like Iceland.

items.title: Einn handtekinn í lögregluaðgerð í Reykholti
items.summary: One person was arrested in Reykholt, Iceland, following a police operation over the weekend. Police seized a significant amount of alleged cannabis plants, cultivation equipment, and narcotics during a house search. The case is currently under investigation.

items.title: Skúli ekki sloppinn: Hæstiréttur vill síðasta orðið
items.summary: The Supreme Court of Iceland has agreed to hear claims related to the bankruptcy of WOW air, including demands for annulment of payments made by the airline and claims for damages against former executives like Skúli Mogensen. The bankruptcy estate alleges that WOW air favored certain creditors before its collapse. This decision means the Supreme Court will provide the final ruling on the interpretation of bankruptcy law and the liability of the former management.
items.why_matters: This case will set a precedent for corporate accountability in major bankruptcies and clarify the application of Icelandic bankruptcy law regarding executive liability and creditor treatment.

items.title: Nýr kafli hefst í íslensku háskólastarfi
items.summary: A new agreement has been signed to establish a university consortium for the University of Iceland, incorporating Hólar University as an affiliated institution. This restructuring, based on new legislation, aims to enhance the competitiveness and quality of Icelandic higher education.
items.why_matters: This policy change will reshape the Icelandic higher education landscape, potentially impacting students, research, and the national workforce.

items.title: Skörp skil: „Við erum ekki sátt með þetta svona“
items.summary: Residents in Vesturbær, Reykjavík, are highly dissatisfied with recent roadwork on Eiðisgrandi by the Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration. They report poor asphalt laying, uneven surfaces, sharp edges, and large puddles that create safety hazards. The contractor states they followed Vegagerðin's instructions for a temporary "wheel track filling" solution.
items.why_matters: This roadwork impacts local residents' daily lives and safety due to poor quality and potential hazards.

items.title: Gúggluðu sjálfsvíg og hnífstungur
items.summary: New evidence has emerged in the Edition Hotel murder case, revealing that Emeric Mancel, one of the deceased, had searched online for suicide methods and knife wounds to the heart shortly before his death. The family's iPad also contained searches related to mass suicides and how to locate the heart in a female body. Ming Ting Mancel, accused of killing her daughter, stated she was largely unaware of her husband's specific searches.
items.why_matters: This new digital evidence provides critical insights into the circumstances surrounding the deaths and is significant for the ongoing murder trial.

items.title: Afmæli Gæslunnar frestað vegna Bandero
items.summary: The Icelandic Coast Guard has postponed its 100th-anniversary celebration in Vestmannaeyjar. The delay is due to ongoing operations involving the ship Bandero, associated with whale conservationist Paul Watson. The celebrations will now take place in the autumn.

items.title: Átti erfitt með að horfa á upptökuna
items.summary: On the fifth day of the 'Edition case' trial, a video recording of Ming Ting Mancel's interrogation was shown in court. Taken shortly after the deaths of her daughter and husband, the video detailed Ming's account of the night her daughter was stabbed and her husband died by suicide, with her assistance. Ming, who is suspected of murder, visibly struggled to watch the recording.
items.why_matters: This article details a significant ongoing murder trial in Iceland, providing insight into a serious domestic crime.

items.title: Hófst allt með örlagaríku snappi
items.summary: The article details the origin of the successful Icelandic musical "Ormstunga," which is based on Gunnlaugs saga Ormstungu. It began when Hafsteinn Níelsson, inspired by "Hamilton," proposed the idea via Snapchat, leading to a collaboration with Ólíver Þorsteinsson. The musical has since been a hit at the National Theatre.

items.title: Handtekin eftir háreysti á Hard Rock: Ekki mismunun
items.summary: A foreign woman filed a discrimination complaint against Hard Rock Café after she and her friends were arrested following a dispute over language and alleged rowdiness. The Gender Equality Complaints Committee ruled against the woman, finding her claims of discrimination due to language difficulties unlikely. The committee noted that menus were available in both Icelandic and English, and the woman did not refute the staff's account of the incident.

items.title: Sváfu hvorki né borðuðu í tvo sólarhringa
items.summary: The Mancel family, involved in the "Edition case," reportedly spent nearly two days without sleep or food in their hotel room before the deaths of Catherine and Emeric Mancel. This information emerged during additional testimony from Ming Ting Mancel, who is accused of killing her daughter. The court proceedings continue.
items.why_matters: This article details the ongoing court proceedings of a serious domestic crime, providing insight into a major legal case.

items.title: Blautþurrkur og dömubindi við Ægisíðu
items.summary: Significant sewage pollution, including wet wipes, sanitary pads, and human feces, has washed ashore at Ægisíða in Reykjavík. This problem is attributed to recent overflows at the utility company Veitur's pumping stations during maintenance and the public flushing non-dissolvable items down toilets. Veitur is aware and will dispatch contractors to clean the affected area.
items.why_matters: This pollution impacts public health and the environment in a popular recreational area, highlighting failures in city infrastructure and public waste disposal practices.

items.title: Bandero ekki komist í nálægð við Hval 8 og Hval 9
items.summary: The Icelandic Coast Guard is actively monitoring the Paul Watson organization's vessel, Bandero, within Icelandic waters, following threats to disrupt whaling operations. The Coast Guard vessel Þór, carrying special forces, is tracking Bandero, which has not yet located the Icelandic whaling ships Hvalur 8 and Hvalur 9. This operation has been in preparation since May, with the Coast Guard ready to intervene if necessary.
items.why_matters: This situation involves a significant deployment of Icelandic law enforcement resources to prevent potential disruption or illegal activity by an activist group against Icelandic industry.

items.title: Þriðjungur skráðra ökutækja á Íslandi með óvirkt neyðarhringikerfi
items.summary: Approximately one-third of registered vehicles in Iceland, totaling around 120,000 cars from 2018-2024, have an inactive eCall emergency system. This critical safety failure is due to the shutdown of 2G and 3G networks, as these vehicles' systems only began supporting 4G in 2025. This means affected cars cannot automatically or manually call emergency services in the event of an accident.
items.why_matters: The failure of these emergency systems could significantly delay critical aid in accidents, potentially leading to more severe injuries or fatalities.

items.title: Telur netverslun með áfengi ólöglega
items.summary: Iceland's Finance Minister states that online alcohol sales are illegal, a position supported by a recent district court ruling against an online store. The EFTA Surveillance Authority is also investigating Iceland's state alcohol monopoly (ÁTVR) following a complaint that it violates the EEA agreement. The legal dispute is ongoing, with the district court ruling currently under appeal.
items.why_matters: This ongoing legal battle could change how alcohol is sold in Iceland, potentially impacting consumer choice and prices.

items.title: Reglugerð um lyfjaakstur væntanleg
items.summary: The Ministry of Infrastructure is finalizing a new regulation on driving under prescription medication, setting impairment limits similar to alcohol. This policy aims to clarify legal uncertainty for drivers and comes after a lawyer challenged past convictions. Stakeholders, including the ADHD Association and the Icelandic Medicines Agency, have provided feedback on the draft.
items.why_matters: This regulation will clarify legal limits for drivers taking prescription medication, potentially affecting many individuals and leading to reviews of past legal cases.

items.title: Höfðu hendur í hári þjófa
items.summary: Police in North Iceland West arrested two foreign men over the weekend, suspected of repeated theft from local stores. During searches of their homes, stolen goods and a small amount of drugs were found. The police are investigating the case.

items.title: Fæðingardeildin lokar í rúmar fimm vikur
items.summary: The maternity ward at the East Iceland Health Institute in Neskaupstaður will close for over five weeks this summer due to necessary renovations of the operating room. This closure, from July 8 to August 14, will affect approximately 20 pregnant women who will need to travel out of the region to give birth. The health institution is assisting affected women with travel and accommodation arrangements.
items.why_matters: This closure means pregnant women in East Iceland will face significant travel and logistical challenges to access essential maternity services this summer.

items.title: Skuldar þjóðinni skýringar
items.summary: Lilja D. Alfreðsdóttir, leader of the Progressive Party, strongly criticizes the government's economic management, stating the situation is "grave." She identifies six policy mistakes that she believes are undermining the fight against inflation and threatening upcoming wage agreements. Alfreðsdóttir argues that the majority of the inflation problem is domestic and criticizes the government's focus on an EU referendum instead of economic issues.
items.why_matters: This critique highlights potential government missteps that could worsen inflation and jeopardize wage agreements, directly impacting citizens' finances.

items.title: Ráðgjöf í Barentshafsþorski hækkar um 16%
items.summary: The Barents Sea cod quota is set to increase by 16% for next year due to a stronger year-class, but this is a temporary rise and the long-term outlook for the cod stock remains poor. This shortage has already led to a 40% year-on-year increase in cod prices, a trend that could worsen with a potential EU ban on Russian cod.
items.why_matters: The fluctuating cod quotas and international policy directly impact the price of cod, contributing to inflation and affecting consumer costs.
items.spin_note: The headline highlights a temporary quota increase, but the article emphasizes that the long-term outlook for cod stock is poor and prices are soaring due to scarcity.

items.title: Bindur vonir við virkjun
items.summary: The mayor of Ísafjarðarbær is hopeful that new legal changes proposed by the Energy Minister will enable the construction of the Hvalárvirkjun power plant in Strandir. This project is considered vital for enhancing energy security and promoting industrial growth in the Westfjords, despite facing opposition from environmental organizations.
items.why_matters: This project could significantly impact energy supply and economic development in the Westfjords region through new infrastructure and policy changes.

items.title: Þór fylgir Bandero eftir vestur af landinu
items.summary: The Icelandic Coast Guard vessel Þór is tracking the ship Bandero, belonging to whale conservationist Paul Watson, west of Iceland. Watson has previously threatened to disrupt the legal whaling operations of Hvalur hf. The Coast Guard deployed special forces personnel to monitor the situation and prevent potential interference.
items.why_matters: The deployment of the Coast Guard and special forces highlights a domestic security response to potential disruption of a legal industry.

items.title: Skipulögðu ferðina án dóttur sinnar
items.summary: A witness testified in the ongoing trial regarding Cathrine Mancel's death at the Edition Hotel, stating that Mancel was informed of her family's Iceland trip with very short notice. The witness, a colleague, described Mancel as usually organized and a 'sunbeam' whose behavior did not change before the trip. The trial continues as investigators examine Mancel's phone.
items.why_matters: This article details developments in a serious criminal case in Iceland.

items.title: Nýta styrkinn í nýjan matsal
items.summary: A golf tournament successfully raised nearly 12.3 million ISK for the Gló summer camp in Reykjadalur, which provides services for disabled children. A significant portion of these funds will be allocated to the construction of a new dining hall at the camp. This year's donation was almost triple the amount raised in the previous year.
items.why_matters: The funds will enable the construction of a new dining hall, improving facilities for disabled children at the summer camp.

items.title: Vestmannaeyingar kalla eftir varaskipi
items.summary: The main ferry to Vestmannaeyjar, Ms. Herjólfur, is operating at half speed due to engine failure, causing significant delays for nearly 1,000 passengers. A temporary backup ferry, Baldur, also experienced technical issues. Residents are calling for a permanent backup ship to be stationed in Vestmannaeyjar, as an older ferry, Herjólfur III, is being prepared for service but its future role is undecided.
items.why_matters: The unreliable ferry service significantly impacts travel and access for the residents of Vestmannaeyjar, highlighting a critical infrastructure need.

items.title: Skorar á ríkissaksóknara að bregðast við
items.summary: A lawyer is challenging the State Prosecutor to review all drug driving cases since 2020, following a recent appeals court acquittal. The court ruling highlighted that the Minister of Infrastructure has failed to issue necessary regulations for drug driving limits, leading to legal uncertainty and potential wrongful convictions.
items.why_matters: The lack of clear regulations on drug driving has led to legal uncertainty and potentially wrongful convictions, impacting individuals and the justice system.

items.title: Sóttu slasaðan göngumann í Hrafntinnusker
items.summary: A rescue team was called to Hrafntinnusker to assist an injured hiker who fell on a trail. The hiker sustained a shoulder injury and was unable to continue due to difficult weather and trail conditions. The rescue team transported the individual to an ambulance.

items.title: Gaf samstarfsfólki sínu „kveðjugjöf“
items.summary: Cathrine Mancel, found dead in an Icelandic hotel, gave handmade "farewell gifts" to colleagues before her trip, according to court testimony in the ongoing "Edition case." Colleagues described her as diligent and happy, and her behavior did not change before her death.
items.why_matters: This article provides details from the ongoing trial concerning a significant death investigation in Iceland.

items.title: Slysið varð í brattri hlíð
items.summary: A hiker was seriously injured in an accident on a steep slope near Hólmavatn in Skagafjörður. Due to the difficult terrain and the nature of her injuries, a large-scale rescue operation involving multiple teams and a Coast Guard helicopter was required to transport her to safety.
items.why_matters: It reports on a significant domestic accident and rescue operation in Iceland.

items.title: Mikill léttir fyrir starfsfólk skólans
items.summary: The Laugalækjaskóli school staff are relieved that long-awaited repairs for leaks and mold in the office hallway will finally proceed this summer. Funding for the project was initially uncertain, causing distress among staff, but the new Reykjavík city council has now secured the necessary funds.
items.why_matters: This decision ensures necessary repairs for a public school building, impacting the health and working conditions of staff and students.

items.title: Malbika 720 metra kafla
items.summary: A 720-meter section of Reykjanesbraut near Sprengisand will be paved tonight, causing temporary road closures and lane reductions. The southbound lane will be closed at Sæbraut, and the northbound lane will be narrowed.
items.why_matters: This construction will cause temporary traffic disruptions on a major road in the capital region.

items.title: Áliti borgarlögmanns stungið ofan í skúffu
items.summary: Reykjavík City's legal opinion, which suggested an agreement with the state for developing state-owned land might involve illegal state aid, was allegedly suppressed. The then-mayor reportedly knew about this opinion before signing the agreement and prevented its presentation to the city council.
items.why_matters: This could lead to legal challenges, financial repercussions for the city, or alter future land development projects in Reykjavík.

items.title: Víðtæk kerfisvilla hjá Skattinum
items.summary: The Icelandic Tax Authority (Skatturinn) has experienced a widespread system error, incorrectly billing many individuals for kilometer fees on vehicles they no longer own. The error affects cars sold earlier in the year, leading to former owners receiving charges for 1,200 kilometers. Skatturinn has confirmed the issue, stating that corrections will be made within a few days, and advises affected individuals to delay payment until the system is updated.
items.why_matters: This system error directly impacts individuals by incorrectly billing them for vehicle fees, requiring them to verify and potentially delay payments.

items.title: 23,8% atvinnuleysi hjá 16 til 24 ára
items.summary: Unemployment among 16-24 year olds in Iceland reached 23.8% in May, significantly higher than the 5.1% for older age groups. This rise is largely due to young people entering the job market for summer jobs. The overall unemployment rate for ages 16-74 was 5.6%.
items.why_matters: This statistic reflects the health of the labor market and can indicate challenges for young people seeking employment.

items.title: Tveir grunaðir um ítrekaðan þjófnað úr verslunum
items.summary: Police in Northwest Iceland arrested two foreign individuals suspected of multiple thefts from local stores. During house searches, stolen goods and a small quantity of drugs were discovered. The police commissioner's office is currently investigating the case.

items.title: Orkuinnviðir Úkraínu kikna undan hita
items.summary: Ukraine's energy infrastructure is struggling under a severe heatwave, leading to power outages across several regions. This crisis is exacerbated by extensive damage from ongoing Russian attacks since 2022, which have severely weakened the power grid. The International Criminal Court has issued arrest warrants for Russian military leaders for war crimes related to these attacks.
items.why_matters: The collapse of Ukraine's energy infrastructure due to war and extreme weather has severe humanitarian consequences and is the subject of international war crime investigations.

items.title: 8 þúsund tonn af malbiki
items.summary: Contractors working for the Icelandic Road Administration have paved 80,000 square meters in the capital area this summer, using 8,000 tons of asphalt. Reykjavíkurborg plans to spend over a billion ISK on paving, with Vegagerðin allocating over 600 million ISK. The work has progressed well due to favorable weather, addressing poor road conditions and deep ruts in some areas.
items.why_matters: This details ongoing public infrastructure spending and improvements to road safety in the capital region.

items.title: Selja mann­virki bæjarins á flug­vellinum á tólf milljónir
items.summary: The Fjallabyggð municipal council has approved the sale of two properties at Siglufjörður airport to the tourism company Viking Heliskiing for 12 million ISK. The properties include an equipment shed and the old airport terminal, built in 1981 and 1973 respectively. The sale was finalized after the buyer removed initial conditions regarding the buildings' structural integrity.
items.why_matters: This decision transfers ownership of municipal airport buildings, impacting local infrastructure and future development at the site.

items.title: 17.07.2026 TILDRA Byggingafélag leitar að verkstjóra á byggingarstað
items.summary: TILDRA Construction Company is seeking a site manager for its diverse building projects. The role involves daily supervision, project planning, coordination with various stakeholders, and ensuring projects meet quality and budget requirements. Candidates should have relevant education and experience in construction site management.

items.title: Ísdal arkitektúr leitar að hönnuði eða tækniteiknara
items.summary: Ísdal arkitektúr & innanhússhönnun is looking to hire a designer or technical drafter. The role involves a variety of architecture and interior design projects, including 2D and 3D technical drawings, material selection, and project coordination. The firm is seeking experienced professionals with relevant education and proficiency in ArchiCAD, offering flexible work arrangements.

items.title: 15.07.2026 Raftákn leitar að tækniteiknara raflagna
items.summary: Raftákn, an Icelandic electrical engineering firm, is hiring an electrical wiring drafter for its Reykjavík or Akureyri offices due to increased activity. The role involves designing electrical systems using Revit and participating in 3D BIM modeling for various projects. The company emphasizes professional development and offers a modern work environment with benefits.

items.title: 01.09.2026 Landsnet kannar markaðinn fyrir færanlegar vinnubúðir úr einingum og gámum
items.summary: Landsnet is conducting a market survey (RFI) for portable work camps and modular units. These units are intended for use in upcoming energy and infrastructure projects. The survey aims to gather information from companies before a formal tender process begins.
items.why_matters: This market survey is a preliminary step for Landsnet's future infrastructure and energy projects, indicating upcoming construction and procurement opportunities.

items.title: Ný hreinsikerfi í sumarbústaði við Þingvallavatn
items.summary: The Health Inspectorate of South Iceland is implementing new wastewater treatment requirements for approximately 600 summer houses around Þingvallavatn to protect the lake's sensitive ecosystem and water quality. Property owners are being informed and guided on suitable solutions, which may include installing new systems or alternative options like incineration toilets, with a focus on tailored approaches rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.
items.why_matters: This initiative will require hundreds of property owners to upgrade their wastewater systems, impacting their costs and property use, and is crucial for protecting the unique ecosystem of Þingvallavatn.

items.title: Mikill léttir fyrir starfsfólk skólans
items.summary: The principal of Laugalækjaskóli expressed great relief that leak and mold repairs will proceed this summer after initial funding issues. Staff were "badly shaken" when funding for the planned repairs on the office corridor seemed to fall through at the last minute. The new city council and parents are credited for their support in ensuring the project goes ahead.
items.why_matters: This decision ensures necessary repairs to a public school, impacting the health and working conditions of staff and students.

items.title: Sér­sveitar­menn um borð í Þór
items.summary: The Icelandic Coast Guard vessel Þór has departed from Reykjavík harbor with special forces on board. The deployment is in response to threats made by Paul Watson against the whaling operations of Hvalur hf., with the aim of protecting the company's whaling ships.
items.why_matters: This deployment signifies a notable domestic security response to threats against an Icelandic industry.

items.title: Selja mann­virki bæjarins á flug­vellinum á tólf milljónir
items.summary: The town council of Fjallabyggð has approved the sale of municipal properties at the Siglufjörður airport. A tourism company, Viking Heliskiing, purchased an equipment shed and the old airport terminal for twelve million Icelandic króna.

items.title: Fræsa og mal­bika Reykja­nes­braut í kvöld
items.summary: The article reports on scheduled road work, including milling and paving, on Reykjanesbraut near Sprengisand. This maintenance is planned for Sunday evening and early Wednesday morning, between 8 PM and 6 AM.

items.title: „Stríðið hefur eyðilagt allt sem við köllum eðlilegt líf“
items.summary: Oleksandra Matvíjtsjúk, a Ukrainian human rights lawyer and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, describes how the war has devastated normal life in Ukraine and the ongoing efforts to document war crimes. She emphasizes the importance of international support and expresses gratitude for the support she felt from the Icelandic people during her visit.

items.title: Skora á stjórnvöld að bjarga endurhæfingunni á Kristnesi
items.summary: Kristnes Hospital in Eyjafjarðarsveit faces an uncertain future and potential closure due to severe mold and moisture damage, forcing the relocation of its rehabilitation and elderly care services. Nearly a thousand people have signed a petition urging the government to fund repairs and save the historic building, which also houses a tuberculosis history museum. The closure threatens vital public services and a cultural site.
items.why_matters: The potential closure of Kristnes Hospital due to structural issues threatens essential rehabilitation services for hundreds of people and the preservation of a significant historical and cultural site.

items.title: 8 þúsund tonn af malbiki
items.summary: Reykjavíkurborg and Vegagerðin are investing over 1.6 billion ISK in asphalt paving projects across the capital area this summer. Contractors have already laid 80,000 square meters of asphalt, with good progress attributed to favorable weather conditions. The work addresses poor road conditions and causes temporary traffic disruptions.
items.why_matters: This project impacts road quality, traffic flow, and safety for drivers in the capital region.

items.title: Tveimur drengjum bjargað úr húsarústum í Venesúela
items.summary: Two powerful earthquakes, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude, struck Venezuela, leading to the rescue of 33 people, including two boys, from collapsed buildings. Over 1,450 deaths have been confirmed, with tens of thousands still missing as international rescue efforts continue. Residents express frustration over the slow pace of the operations.
items.why_matters: The earthquakes have caused widespread devastation, significant loss of life, and an ongoing humanitarian crisis in Venezuela.

items.title: Þriggja bíla árekstur við Gullinbrú
items.summary: A three-car collision occurred at Gullinbrú in Reykjavík, resulting in one person being transported to the emergency room for examination. Three vehicles sustained damage in the incident. Firefighters also responded to a separate cooking-related smoke alarm.

items.title: Innlegg í gerð búvörusamninga
items.summary: The Association of Business Owners has proposed eight measures to the government aimed at lowering food prices in Iceland, which are currently 55% higher than the EU average. These proposals, including reducing customs protection on food imports and shifting farmer support to direct payments, will be considered during the drafting of new agricultural agreements.
items.why_matters: These policy proposals could significantly impact food prices and the cost of living for consumers in Iceland.

items.title: Ætti að grafa Einar upp ásamt Jónasi?
items.summary: Two Icelandic MPs debated the potential exhumation of poet Einar Benediktsson's remains alongside Jónas Hallgrímsson's. The discussion also covered the future of the national burial site, which one MP noted was established during the independence struggle and has ancient relics beneath it.

items.title: Framkvæmd sem margborgaði sig
items.summary:
The article discusses the 1972 construction of the Vesturlandsvegur road in Kollafjörður using concrete, which proved highly durable, lasting 54 years

 an Icelandic record. Despite initial controversy over its higher cost compared to asphalt, its longevity demonstrated significant long-term value.
items.why_matters: This article highlights the long-term benefits and cost-effectiveness of durable infrastructure choices, which is relevant for current planning decisions.

items.title: „Nokkurn veginn allt“ fallið með ís­lenskum sjávarút­vegi síðustu misseri
items.summary: The Icelandic fisheries sector has experienced significant success recently, driven by substantial price increases for its products, a trend expected to continue. A new analysis highlights aquaculture, particularly salmon feed production, as a key long-term growth area for companies like Síldarvinnslan, moving beyond traditional fishing.
items.why_matters: The strong performance of a major Icelandic industry can influence the national economy and future investment.

items.title: Einn fluttur á spítala eftir líkams­á­rás
items.summary: Police in the capital region responded to a report of an assault in downtown Reykjavík. One individual was taken to the hospital with significant injuries following the incident.

items.title: „Það koma bara færri“
items.summary: Cruise ship arrivals to smaller towns in Northeast Iceland have sharply decreased after a lodging tax was imposed. A tourism operator states that some towns now receive no ship visits, and the tax provides little to no benefit to the state treasury.
items.why_matters: This policy impacts local economies reliant on tourism and the effectiveness of government revenue generation.

items.title: Gæslan á leið að hvalveiðiskipunum: „Við munum vernda líf og limi“
items.summary: The Icelandic Coast Guard has deployed its vessel Þór to protect whaling ships from threats by the Paul Watson organization (Sea Shepherd). The activist group entered Icelandic waters and threatened to stop the whaling operations. The Coast Guard director stated they will ensure the safety of all parties involved.
items.why_matters: The Coast Guard's intervention aims to prevent potential conflict or accidents between Icelandic whaling vessels and foreign activist groups in Icelandic waters.

items.title: Segist ekki ætla að stefna áhöfn í hættu
items.summary: Activist Paul Watson's ship, Bandero, is in Icelandic waters with the stated goal of stopping whaling without endangering crews. The Icelandic Coast Guard has dispatched a patrol ship to monitor the whaling vessels. Watson denies plans to break laws, despite referencing a past incident where he organized the sinking of whaling boats.
items.why_matters: This situation involves a direct confrontation between an activist group and Icelandic authorities over whaling operations, with potential for disruption and law enforcement involvement.

items.title: Óvissa ríkir um skipaumferð í Hormússundi
items.summary: Significant uncertainty surrounds shipping in the Strait of Hormuz due to an unstable ceasefire between Iran and the US, leading to continued attacks and chaos for shipping companies. Companies face a dilemma in choosing safe routes, fearing both Iranian attacks and Western sanctions. This situation creates disorder and danger for ship crews.
items.why_matters: Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz can impact global supply chains and potentially contribute to increased shipping costs and inflation.

items.title: Stór hluti framhaldsskólanema spilar fjárhættuspil – kallað eftir auknum forvörnum
items.summary: A new survey reveals that 40% of Icelandic high school students have gambled in the past year, with higher rates among young men. A University of Iceland docent highlights the associated risks, including debt and mental health issues, and calls for increased prevention efforts. The study also notes a significant rise in loneliness among young people.
items.why_matters: Widespread youth gambling leads to serious issues like debt and mental health problems, requiring societal policy intervention.

items.title: Spretti út úr búðinni með peysu í hendi
items.summary: A young man shoplifted a sweater from a 66°North store on Laugavegur in Reykjavík in broad daylight. Store staff pursued him but he escaped, and police have been called.

items.title: Áhöfn Bandero gaf upp staðsetningu
items.summary: The Icelandic Coast Guard has started receiving manual location updates from the vessel "Bandero," associated with anti-whaling activist Paul Watson. The ship, which entered Icelandic economic waters, had previously reported its automatic location equipment was broken. The Coast Guard had requested hourly updates, which are now being provided.

items.title: Nokkuð slasaður eftir líkamsárás í miðbænum
items.summary: A police log summary reports on several incidents in the capital region. A man was hospitalized after an assault in downtown Reykjavik, and police are searching for a suspect. Other incidents included another fight, a restaurant break-in leading to an arrest, and a bicycle accident.

items.title: Þór lagður af stað: Sérsveitarmenn um borð
items.summary: The Icelandic Coast Guard vessel Þór has departed Reykjavík with special forces onboard, heading towards Icelandic whaling ships. This deployment is in response to threats from anti-whaling activist Paul Watson, whose ship has entered Icelandic economic waters. The Coast Guard aims to protect lives and prevent potential incidents.
items.why_matters: This deployment aims to prevent potential international conflict or criminal acts against Icelandic commercial interests and ensure safety at sea.

items.title: Hafa ekki gefið Land­helgis­gæslunni upp stað­setningu Bandero
items.summary: The crew of the activist ship Bandero, associated with Paul Watson, has refused to provide its location to the Icelandic Coast Guard after entering Iceland's exclusive economic zone. The chairman of "Friends of Whales" has expressed concern about the ship's presence.
items.why_matters: This incident involves a foreign vessel potentially violating maritime regulations within Iceland's economic zone, requiring action from the Icelandic Coast Guard.

items.title: Mikil­vægt fram­fara­skref fyrir allt landið
items.summary: The article announces the groundbreaking ceremony for a new wing at Akureyri Hospital. This marks the formal start of a significant healthcare construction project in rural Iceland, which has been a long-term goal.
items.why_matters: This project represents a major investment in healthcare infrastructure outside the capital region.

items.title: „Ætlum rétt að vona að þessi tímalína standist“
items.summary: The CEO of the Herjólfur ferry service reports ongoing delays in the ferry's repairs but expresses confidence in transport for the upcoming Þjóðhátíð festival in Vestmannaeyjar. Despite some cancellations with another ferry, Baldur, post-event transport from the islands has been managed effectively.
items.why_matters: This impacts the reliability of essential transport infrastructure for residents and visitors to Vestmannaeyjar, especially during peak event times.

items.title: Hnífstunguárás á Riddaranum í Engihjalla
items.summary: A man was stabbed at a bar in Kópavogur, Iceland, last night. Police arrested the attacker, who spent the night in custody, while the victim was taken to the emergency room.
items.why_matters: This incident represents a serious violent crime in the capital region.

items.title: 10 ár frá Brexit: Sannfærður um að Bretar gangi aftur í ESB
items.summary: The article marks 10 years since the Brexit vote, noting a significant shift in public opinion with a majority of Britons now believing it was a mistake and wanting to rejoin the EU. Economists estimate the UK's GDP is 6-8% lower, making the average Briton poorer, than if it had remained in the EU. A professor from the London School of Economics is convinced the UK will be back in the EU or on its way within the next decade.
items.why_matters: This article discusses the long-term economic and political consequences of a major country leaving the EU, offering insights into the real-world impact of such policy decisions.

items.title: Hafa ekki gefið upp staðsetningu sína þvert á kröfu Gæslunnar
items.summary: The Paul Watson Foundation's ship, Bandero, has entered Iceland's economic zone to protest whaling but has refused to report its location to the Icelandic Coast Guard, claiming its tracking device is broken. The Coast Guard has demanded hourly location updates for maritime safety, which the crew has ignored. This defiance of regulations is unusual and concerns law enforcement and search and rescue protocols.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights a direct challenge to Icelandic maritime law enforcement and safety protocols by an international activist group.

items.title: Bæði Baldur og Herjólfur sigla á takmörkuðu afli
items.summary: Two key ferries, Herjólfur and Baldur, serving the Westman Islands, are experiencing significant operational issues, leading to reduced schedules and capacity. Herjólfur has been operating on limited power since April due to a delayed repair, and Baldur, brought in to assist, now has an engine malfunction. These disruptions have led to a 4% increase in Herjólfur's tariffs for passengers.
items.why_matters: The disruptions and tariff increase directly impact travel costs and reliability for those using ferry services to and from the Westman Islands.

items.title: Þorskverð 40% hærra
items.summary: Fish prices, particularly for cod, have risen by nearly 40% in the past year. This increase is attributed to a weakening cod stock in the Barents Sea, leading to reduced quotas for Norway and Russia, and new EU sanctions against Russia that include a ban on cod sales.
items.why_matters: Rising fish prices contribute to overall inflation, directly affecting household budgets and the Icelandic economy.

items.title: Kristrún kynnti sér Eyjagöng
items.summary: Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir visited Vestmannaeyjar to review the progress of the planned Eyjagöng tunnel project. Soil sample drilling for the tunnels was recently completed, and the PM met with the project's CEO to discuss the research and next steps.
items.why_matters: This project represents a significant infrastructure development for the Vestmannaeyjar region, potentially improving connectivity and transport.

items.title: Reistu verksmiðju á 69 dögum
items.summary: An American startup has rapidly built and begun operating a pilot plant in Húsavík, Iceland, in just 69 days. This facility is the first globally to use geothermal energy directly for hydrogen production, aiming to reduce costs for eco-friendly fuel.
items.why_matters: This project could advance green energy production and establish new industrial capabilities in Iceland.

items.title: Watson daufheyrist enn við skipunum Gæslunnar
items.summary: Paul Watson's ship, Bandero, has reportedly turned off its location transponder and is not providing its position to the Icelandic Coast Guard, despite requests. The Coast Guard considers this a safety concern for seafarers and is continuing its surveillance within Iceland's economic zone.
items.why_matters: This incident highlights ongoing challenges in maritime surveillance and safety within Iceland's economic zone.

items.title: Trump yfirgefur landið
items.summary: Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner have departed Iceland after a private visit. Their arrival earlier in the week had drawn attention, with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirming standard assistance for their non-official stay. They reportedly stayed at a luxury hotel in Fljótin.

items.title: Útboð að hefjast í rannsóknahúsinu
items.summary: Tenders for interior work on the new Landspítali research building at Hringbraut are set to begin in July, with construction expected to start in the autumn. This project is part of a larger development that includes an extension to Læknagarður for the University of Iceland's Health Sciences department, and is located along the future Borgarlína route.
items.why_matters: This project signifies a major development in the capital region's public infrastructure and facilities.

items.title: Stangarbærinn minnir á gróðurhús
items.summary: The Stöng farm in Þjórsárdalur is experiencing significant plant growth inside its new, clear covering, which was opened in 2024. The design of the roof, resembling a greenhouse, has led to an unexpected abundance of vegetation. The Cultural Heritage Agency is now working on solutions, including placing pumice on the floor, to address the issue and preserve the historical site.
items.why_matters: The design flaw in the new covering impacts the preservation of a significant historical Icelandic building.

items.title: Kjarnasögun ehf. fær fráveituverkefni á Þingeyri
items.summary: Kjarnasögun ehf. has been awarded a contract by Ísafjarðarbær municipal council to renew the sewage and water pipe systems in Þingeyri. The project involves laying new surface water and sewer pipes, and renewing existing water lines. This decision followed a tender process where Kjarnasögun ehf. submitted the sole bid, which was 108.5% of the estimated cost.
items.why_matters: This project will upgrade essential water and sewage infrastructure for the community of Þingeyri.

items.title: Eitt flóknasta niðurrifsverkefni Íslandssögunnar
items.summary: Grindavík, once a lively town of nearly 4,000 residents, is now largely empty with only about 900 registered inhabitants following natural disasters and the November 2023 evacuation. The article describes the extensive impact on the town's buildings and population, setting the stage for what is called one of Iceland's most complex demolition projects.
items.why_matters: This article describes the ongoing severe impact of natural disasters on Grindavík, necessitating major demolition and reconstruction efforts, which represents a significant municipal planning challenge and cost.
items.spin_note: The headline claims a complex demolition project, but the body only describes the current state of Grindavík and the impact of the disaster, without detailing the project itself.

items.title: Tilboði Íshnits ehf. hafnað í gatnagerð í Bláskógabyggð
items.summary: The Bláskógabyggð municipal council rejected a bid from Íshnit ehf. for a road construction project, citing the company's failure to meet professional and technical qualification requirements. The council is now evaluating the next lowest bid from Ketilbjörn ehf. to select a contractor who meets all criteria.
items.why_matters: This decision impacts the progress and contractor selection for a local road construction project.

items.title: Framkvæmd sem margborgaði sig
items.summary: An article highlights the exceptional durability of the concrete pavement on Vesturlandsvegur through Kollafjörður, constructed in 1972. The road surface lasted an Icelandic record of 54 years before being resurfaced this summer. A former concrete company CEO attributes this longevity to the use of high-quality, non-alkaline concrete.

items.title: Milljarða fjárfestingar fram undan á Keflavíkurflugvelli
items.summary: Isavia is planning multi-billion króna investments at Keflavík Airport, including a 22 billion ISK connecting building and a 12 billion ISK de-icing area. These projects aim to enhance passenger experience, improve operational efficiency, and prepare for future growth. Upgrades to baggage handling and security screening systems, along with hotel development, are also part of the extensive plans.
items.why_matters: These significant infrastructure investments will impact the capacity, efficiency, and passenger experience at Iceland's primary international airport for years to come.

items.title: Mats­gerðirnar einar ekki nægar til að sanna akstur undir á­hrifum slævandi lyfja
items.summary: The Icelandic Court of Appeals has reduced a man's prison sentence from four to three months. He was initially convicted of driving under the influence of sedative drugs multiple times, but the appeals court acquitted him of those specific charges.
items.why_matters: This case clarifies the legal standard for proving driving under the influence of sedative drugs in Iceland, indicating that expert assessments alone may not be sufficient.

items.title: Réðst að hópi drengja í sund­laug
items.summary: A man reportedly attacked a group of boys in a swimming pool in western Reykjavík after they collided with him and his son on a waterslide. The incident was recorded in the police log.

items.title: Tala látinna hækkar og gremja í­búa eykst
items.summary: The death toll from two major earthquakes in Venezuela last week has risen to 1,430, with an additional 68,900 people reported missing. The 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude quakes devastated the South American nation.
items.why_matters: This is a major humanitarian disaster with a significant loss of life and many missing.

items.title: Mickelson sýndi eigin­konu keppi­nautar nektar­mynd af sér
items.summary: Renowned golfer Phil Mickelson is accused by Ashley Perez, the ex-wife of fellow golfer Pat Perez, of showing her nude photos of himself. She claims he also asked her to meet him while her then-husband was asleep.

items.title: Hve­nær ætlum við að taka mál­efni heimilis­lausra al­var­lega?
items.summary: This opinion piece criticizes the Icelandic public sector's approach to homelessness, arguing that providing shelter and support should be the government's responsibility, not solely that of aid organizations. The author highlights the ongoing debate about housing for Samhjálp's soup kitchen as an example of this systemic issue.
items.why_matters: This article discusses the government's role in housing policy for vulnerable populations, which directly impacts social welfare and public spending.

items.title: Réðst að hópi drengja í sundlaug
items.summary: The article details several incidents from the police log in the capital area over a 12-hour period. Key events include a man attacking boys in a swimming pool, a serious assault at a sports bar, and multiple drunk driving incidents. Police also investigated a suspected scam against tourists and youths breaking into a school.
items.why_matters: This article highlights ongoing public safety concerns and criminal activity in the capital region.

items.title: Sundlaugar áfram opnar til 22 um helgar í haust
items.summary: Reykjavík City's Sports and Outdoor Council has permanently extended the opening hours of city swimming pools until 10 PM on weekends, starting September 1st. This decision, initially a trial, is part of a policy to increase access to public pools and is estimated to cost 31 million ISK annually.
items.why_matters: This decision impacts public access to city facilities and has a recurring cost for Reykjavík City's budget.

items.title: Villistrákarnir: „Ein af merkari bókum bandarískra bókmennta á síðustu öld“
items.summary: This article reviews the new Icelandic translation of William S. Burroughs' "The Wild Boys," highlighting its historical significance in counter-culture and its challenging literary style. It discusses the book's long journey to Icelandic publication and its influence on various artists, including Icelandic visual artist Örn Karlsson.

items.title: Guðmundur í Brim bætir við sig töluverðum kvóta með kaupum á útgerð á æskuslóðum
items.summary: Guðmundur Kristjánsson, CEO of Brim, has acquired Þórsnes ehf., a fishing company in Stykkishólmur, through a holding company. This acquisition significantly increases his fishing quota holdings, with Þórsnes owning substantial assets and fishing rights. The current CEO of Þórsnes will remain in his role.
items.why_matters: This acquisition consolidates significant fishing quotas under a major industry player, impacting the structure of the Icelandic fisheries sector.

items.title: Réðst á hóp drengja sem renndi sér of nærri
items.summary: The article details various incidents reported to the Icelandic police over the past 24 hours. Key events include a man assaulting boys at a downtown swimming pool, attempted school break-ins, and multiple accidents involving drunk drivers of small vehicles. Police also responded to neighbor disputes and suspected rental fraud involving tourists.

items.title: Óánægðir með fyrirkomulag veiðanna
items.summary: Eider farmers in Norðurþing are dissatisfied with the municipality's fox and mink hunting arrangements, claiming significant damage to their eider colonies due to insufficient pest control and poor communication with hunters. The local council is reviewing the hunting agreements. Professional hunters also complain that their wages have not kept pace with inflation since 1996.
items.why_matters: This article highlights how local government policy and inflation can directly impact the livelihoods of specific groups of workers and farmers.

items.title: Banna viðtöl og myndbandsupptökur
items.summary: The District Prosecutor's office will ban all video recordings and interviews on its premises. This decision follows an incident where a promotional video by an Israeli tech company, filmed at the office, inadvertently displayed the names of defendants. The prosecutor emphasized that staff had specifically instructed the company to avoid showing any personally identifiable information.
items.why_matters: This policy change aims to prevent future breaches of sensitive data and protect the privacy of individuals involved in legal cases.

items.title: Sky lagoon sýknað af kröfu starfsmanns sem rann
items.summary: The Reykjanes District Court acquitted Sky Lagoon in a lawsuit brought by a former employee who suffered a concussion after slipping on a wet changing room floor in 2021. The employee, who sustained permanent disability, sought compensation, but the court ruled the incident was an accident and not due to employer negligence. Despite previous reports of slippery floors and other slips, the court found Sky Lagoon had taken sufficient measures to mitigate risk.
items.why_matters: This ruling clarifies employer liability in workplace accidents in Iceland, even when serious injuries occur, if negligence cannot be proven.

items.title: Sálin kom saman í fyrsta sinn í rúman ára­tug
items.summary: The Icelandic band Sálin hans Jóns míns reunited for the first time in over a decade for two sold-out anniversary concerts at Harpa. The event celebrated lead singer Stefán Hilmarsson's 60th birthday and 40 years in music.

items.title: For­eldrar standi eftir „einir, ör­magna og án stuðnings“
items.summary: A mother whose son received treatment in South Africa criticizes Iceland's child protection system, stating it fails children most in need. She highlights that a new National Audit Office report on welfare law implementation confirms what parents already know, urging for action rather than just drafting new laws.
items.why_matters: This article highlights systemic failures in Iceland's child protection system, impacting vulnerable children and their families.

items.title: Sex ís­lenskir söngvarar ráðnir til Þjóðaróperunnar
items.summary: The National Opera has announced the hiring of six Icelandic soloists. These singers, including sopranos, a mezzo-soprano, a tenor, a baritone, and a bass, will join the national institution.

items.title: Verður Ís­land brot­hætt byggð?
items.summary: The article argues that Iceland significantly overestimates its negotiating power in potential talks to join the European Union. It states that Iceland's small population means it cannot expect to change the EU's established rules.
items.why_matters: Potential EU accession talks could significantly alter Iceland's economic and political landscape.

items.title: Festa lengri opnunar­tíma lauganna um helgar í sessi
items.summary: Reykjavík City's Sports and Outdoor Life Council has approved a proposal to extend the weekend opening hours of all city swimming pools. Starting September 1st, pools will remain open until 10 PM on weekends.
items.why_matters: This decision impacts public access to recreational facilities in the capital region.

items.title: „Málið er í öllu til­liti afar ó­heppi­legt“
items.summary: Benedikt Bogason, President of the Supreme Court, stated that a case involving Margrét Friðriksdóttir and the Lawyers' Disciplinary Committee could undermine public trust in the courts and legal professionals. He stressed the increasing importance of the rule of law and the necessity for citizens to have faith in these institutions.
items.why_matters: This issue concerns the fundamental integrity of Iceland's legal system and public trust in its institutions.

items.title: Slösuð göngu­kona flutt með þyrlunni
items.summary: An injured hiker was rescued by the Icelandic Coast Guard helicopter after falling near Hólmavatn, southeast of Sauðárkrókur. The incident occurred earlier in the evening.

items.title: Yfir fjórtán hundruð hafa fundist látin
items.summary: A devastating earthquake in Venezuela has resulted in over 1,400 confirmed deaths and thousands more missing. International rescue teams are on the ground, but residents are frustrated by the slow pace of recovery efforts and lack of equipment. Many are digging by hand to find loved ones.
items.why_matters: This event highlights the devastating impact of major natural disasters and the challenges of international humanitarian response.

items.title: Ógeðfellt að kenna leiðangur við skemmdarverk
items.summary: Paul Watson's Captain Paul Watson Foundation is sending a ship to Iceland to disrupt whaling. Árni Finnsson, chairman of the Icelandic Nature Conservation Association, criticizes Watson's methods, calling them "disgusting" and counterproductive. He references Watson's past act of sinking two whaling boats in Reykjavík in 1986, stating such vandalism only benefits the whaling company.
items.why_matters: The debate reflects ongoing tensions in environmental activism against Icelandic whaling, and could influence future protest actions.

items.title: Göngukona slasaðist við Hólmavatn
items.summary: A hiker was injured near Hólmavatn in Skagafjörður and required a helicopter rescue by the Icelandic Coast Guard. The woman was transported to Landspítalinn in Fossvogur for medical attention.

items.title: Bandero ekki með kveikt á staðsetningarbúnaði
items.summary: A ship named Bandero, associated with whale conservationist Paul Watson, entered Icelandic economic waters without its automatic identification system (AIS) turned on. The Icelandic Coast Guard spotted the vessel and requested hourly manual position updates after the crew claimed the AIS was broken. This incident highlights a regulatory and safety concern for maritime traffic.

items.title: Skip Watsons komið inn fyrir 200 mílurnar
items.summary: Paul Watson's anti-whaling ship, Bandero, has entered Iceland's 200-mile economic zone, with Watson claiming the Icelandic Coast Guard is monitoring them. The group intends to prevent Hvalur hf.'s planned whaling this summer and has threatened direct action if whaling ships are deployed.
items.why_matters: This situation could lead to direct confrontations at sea, legal action, and international attention regarding Iceland's whaling industry.

items.title: Segir niðurstöðu Ríkisendurskoðunar sláandi
items.summary: The National Audit Office has released a report indicating that the Icelandic state is failing to implement the Children's Well-being Act, passed in 2021. A mother, whose son sought addiction treatment abroad due to domestic shortages, highlights that the law has not led to increased resources or shorter waiting lists for vulnerable children. The report confirms systemic failures and a lack of accountability in providing essential services for children with complex needs.
items.why_matters: The government's failure to implement the Children's Well-being Act means vulnerable children and their families continue to lack essential support and services.

items.title: Watson skipað að kveikja á staðsetningarbúnaði
items.summary: The Icelandic Coast Guard intercepted Paul Watson's ship, Bandero, as it entered Iceland's economic zone because its location device was off. Watson, a prominent anti-whaling activist, has stated his intention to disrupt whaling in Iceland. The Coast Guard ordered hourly position reports and affirmed they would respond to threats to life and health.
items.why_matters: This involves Icelandic authorities enforcing maritime regulations against an activist known for disruptive actions, potentially impacting Iceland's whaling industry.

items.title: Sóttu slasaða göngukonu
items.summary: An injured hiker was rescued by a Coast Guard helicopter near Hólmavatn, southeast of Sauðárkrókur. The woman was transported to the emergency room at Landspítalinn in Fossvogur, though the severity of her injuries was not confirmed.

items.title: Fjöldi ferða Baldurs fellur niður
items.summary: The Baldur ferry service between Vestmannaeyjar and Landeyjahöfn has announced multiple cancellations for Sunday and all scheduled trips for Monday. These disruptions are attributed to unforeseen circumstances, and affected passengers are advised to contact the ferry operator for rebooking.
items.why_matters: This disruption will significantly impact travel plans for many individuals and potentially the movement of goods to and from the Westman Islands.

items.title: Þjóðin föst í Groundhog Day krónunnar
